O.outcome_detail: testing throughput and administration time

cells.quote: Schoolmen generally have come to see the advantages of the Binet measurements of intelligence, but the necessity of examining each pupil individually has put such a time cost on the use of the scale as to restrict its employment to special cases. O.outcome_detail: satisfaction as a measure of intelligence

cells.quote: As a result the committee has now before it and will shortly be able to offer to the country two series of group tests of general intelligence of a high degree of reliability that have been carefully tested out on large groups of children, and that give as satisfactory a measure of intelligence as any scale now available.
cells.note: This is the editor's narrative assertion of reliability and measurement adequacy, not a reported experimental comparison with an effect size.

O.outcome_detail: test satisfaction and measurement reliability

cells.quote: After detailed study the committee selected some twenty tests and gave these a careful trial on five thousand children. From these tests two series were selected which seemed to give the most satisfaction, and in order to perfect the procedure and to still further check up on the results the tests were tried on several thousand more children.
cells.note: The text reports a selection and re-trial procedure but provides no statistical comparison, effect size, assignment method, learner age, setting details, or duration.
